previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and heart failure, was admitted after a fall down stairs, sustaining multiple right rib fractures, a pulmonary contusion, and a lumbar spine fracture. He developed acute kidney injury likely due to contrast exposure and volume depletion, leading to toxic-metabolic encephalopathy. He required temporary hemodialysis via a right internal jugular catheter, which was removed after renal recovery. A Citrobacter koseri infection in the transplanted kidney was treated with ceftriaxone followed by oral ciprofloxacin. His mental status improved with dialysis and infection treatment. His pain was managed conservatively, and he was weaned off narcotics. He completed adjustments to his immunosuppressive, anticoagulant, and insulin regimens. He was discharged to an extended care facility with a vancomycin taper for recurrent C. diff, follow-up plans for fecal transplant, and instructions to monitor kidney function and INR.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old male with history of atrial 
fibrillation on Coumadin, ESRD status post LURT in ___ (on 
prednisone, MMF, tacrolimus), recurrent C. diff infections 
recently completed PO vancomycin taper on ___, CAD, HTN, 
HLD, DM2, severe PVD, and prostate Ca s/p XRT who initially 
presented with abdominal pain and shortness of breath, with CT 
findings demonstrating colitis in the cecum and ascending colon 
and proctitis, with suspected ischemic cause and acute on 
chronic diastolic CHF. Hospital course complicated by UTI and 
?HAP now on augmentin per ID recommendation. Patient also 
underwent colonoscopy which was notable for apthous ulcers and 
cecum and ascending colon, transverse and rectal polyps, and 
likely radiation proctitis. 

ACUTE ISSUES
============
#Abdominal Pain
#Colitis 
#Proctitis - Patient has a history of recurrent C. difficile 
infections, recently completing PO vancomycin taper on ___, 
who presented with a one-day history of dull periumbilical 
abdominal pain after PO intake. CT abdomen and pelvis 
demonstrated cecal and ascending colon colitis and proctitis, 
with possible infectious versus ischemic etiology given 
distribution. Given long-standing C. difficile history, 
infectious colitis was considered, however patient initially had 
no evidence of diarrhea, thought unlikely to have C. difficile 
at this time. In consideration of immunocompromised state, 
patient was initially started on Cipro, Flagyl, and PO 
vancomycin for C. difficile prophylaxis. 

Transplant ID was consulted and given immunosuppressed state, 
stool cultures and O&P were obtained which were negative. CMV VL 
was also negative. Transplant ID thought that this is unlikely 
to be infectious in etiology given afebrile, without 
leukocytosis on admission. Given history of severe PVD and 
temporal nature between onset of abdominal pain after PO intake, 
abdominal pain was thought to be more consistent with ischemic 
colitis. Antibiotics were subsequently discontinued, and patient 
was later switched to augmentin per below for enterococcus UTI 
and possible HAP.

CT findings were thought to be more consistent with ischemic 
colitis, however patient was unable to go for CTA abdomen given 
CKD 4 with previous history of CIN/ATN on previous 
hospitalization. GI was consulted. Patient underwent 
colonoscopy, which showed abnormal mucosa with angiectasia in 
the rectum and oozing likely radiation proctitis status post 
biopsy. Also found to have aphthous ulcers in the cecum and 
ascending colon status post biopsy. Incidentally found to have 
transverse colon and rectal polyps, which were not removed given 
patient was on anticoagulation, and diverticulosis of the 
sigmoid colon. Patient will require nonurgent repeat colonoscopy 
for polyp removal, with consideration of holding anti-platelets 
and anti-coagulation prior to repeat colonoscopy.

#Acute on Chronic HFpEF
#Bilateral Pleural Effusions
#Pericardial Effusion - Patient initially presented with SOB and 
orthopnea in the setting of having recently held torsemide on 
last admission due to orthostatic hypotension and patient was 
noted to be auto diuresing at time of previous discharge. 
Admission CXR demonstrating pulmonary edema and CT showed 
moderate right pleural and small left pleural effusion with 
small pericardial effusion. Trigger likely in the setting of 
having previously held torsemide on last admission and also with 
dietary indiscretion. No evidence of cardiac tamponade. EKG 
demonstrating non-specific ST/T wave changes with early P waves, 
otherwise unchanged from prior EKGs. Troponins were 0.02 and 
0.03 at baseline with flat CK-MB, making ischemic etiology of 
presentation less likely. Patient received intermittent IV Lasix 
100 mg boluses and discharged on torsemide 40mg PO QD. Discharge 
weight 76.1kg. 

#Possible HAP - Patient was noted to have worsening leukocytosis 
with peak 11.3, new 2L O2 requirement, with repeat chest x-ray 
demonstrating worsening opacity at the right lung base, with 
resolution of left-sided pleural effusion. Patient remained 
afebrile, however given concern for underlying healthcare 
acquired pneumonia, patient was started on vancomycin and 
cefepime, which was later descalated to augmentin. Patient was 
also continued on PO vancomycin for C. Diff prophylaxis. Plan 
for 7 day course of antibiotics total, augmentin to be completed 
on ___. Will continue vancomycin 125mg QID for 2 weeks 
following completion of augmentin (end ___.

#UTI - Although asymptomatic, urine cultures grew ampicillin 
sensitive and vancomycin resistant enterococcus. Initially 
started on amoxicillin, however later switched to augmentin per 
above in order to cover VRE and HAP. 

#Sub-theapeutic INR 
#History of Atrial Fibrillation s/p DCCV - Patient has a history 
of AF s/p DCCV with conversion to NSR. EKG demonstrating NSR 
without AF. Maintained on home warfarin 1.5mg PO QD and was 
subtherapeutic INR of 1.8. Was not started on heparin gtt given 
INR was subtherapeutic on last admission and also currently in 
NSR. Warfarin was dosed daily and patient received FFP prior to 
colonoscopy given INR was 3. Patient was also continued on rate 
control with carvedilol 25 mg PO BID. Discharged on warfarin 
1.5mg PO QD.

#HTN - Patient was initially hypertensive on admission to 182/65 
and was continued on home carvedilol 25 mg PO BID.

#ESRD s/p LURT
#CKD IV - Baseline Cr is ___ with Cr during admission lower 
than previous baseline. Renal US showed no evidence of 
hydronephrosis on admission. He was continued on home prednisone 
5mg PO QD, MMF 250mg PO BID, and tacrolimus 2mg PO BID.

silhouette is unchanged.
